text.p: British facilities and construction group Jarvis Plc said on Thursday its two proposed acquisitions -- costing 55 million stg -- would bring a "considerable enhancement" to next year's earnings.

The company said earlier it planned to acquire Fastline Group Ltd, a track renewal firm operating mainly in north and east of England and buy out the remaining 50 percent it did not own in another UK track firm, Relayfast Ltd.
"This year the effect will be marginal but next year we are hoping there will be considerable enhancement to our earnings," Paris Moayedi, Jarvis' chief executive told Reuters in an interview.
Jarvis is paying 50 million stg for Fastline which employs about 1,200 people and another five million stg for gaining full control of Relayfast which has 740 people.

A sum of between 2.7 million and 8.3 million stg will be paid in Jarvis shares while the balance will be in cash. The company also announced a rights issue of convertible unsecured loan stock of 64.1 million stg.

Moayedi said the acquisitions would help it to secure more contracts, especially from rail infrastructure firm Railtrack Plc which has embarked on a 10-year, 15 billion stg revamp plan for Britain's railway tracks and stations.
Jarvis, on its own, secured contracts worth 150 million stg from Railtrack last year while Fastline and Relayfast jointly executed contracts worth 120 million stg.
"The acquisitions give us geographical spread and access to heavy plant and machinery and also give us additional skills...," Moayedi said.
Jarvis estimates the market for track renewal and upgrading work for Railtrack was in excess of 300 million stg in 1996/97.
"This figure is forecast to increase substantially, particularly as major new projects such as the West Coast Main Line modernisation and Thameslink 2000 develop," the company said.

Moayedi said all its operating divisions had showed an improved performance so far this year. "All of our operating divisions are operating at better levels of turnover and obtaining higher margins," he said.
"We are ahead of previous year's performance at this stage," he added.
Relayfast incurred an operating loss of 3.4 million stg last year but Jarvis is restucturing its management and hopes to turn it around soon.
